gaps.sentence: There was ___ fog at the airport all morning.
gaps.explanation: thick fog (or dense fog) is the standard collocation; 'strong fog' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: A sudden clap of thunder ___ the silence.
gaps.explanation: break the silence is the fixed collocation for ending a quiet period.

gaps.sentence: The doctor has ___ detailed records of every patient since 1990.
gaps.explanation: keep records (of something) is the fixed collocation for storing information.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ great progress since she changed schools.
gaps.explanation: make progress is the collocation; after 'has' the past participle 'made' is needed.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ your word, people will trust you.
gaps.explanation: keep your word means to do what you promised.

gaps.sentence: The neighbours ___ a loud argument in the garden last night.
gaps.explanation: have an argument (with somebody) is the fixed collocation for quarrelling.

gaps.sentence: Most children learn to ___ the time before they start school.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: ___ the time (read a clock)
gaps.explanation: tell the time means to be able to read a clock; it is a fixed expression.

gaps.sentence: The crash left several passengers seriously ___.
gaps.explanation: seriously injured is the standard collocation describing bad injuries in accidents.
